pool.q: Without the natural greenhouse effect, what would Earth's average temperature be?
pool.explain: Some greenhouse effect is natural and essential; human emissions intensify it.
pool.evidence: Without the greenhouse effect, the average temperature of the earth would be about -2°F rather than the 57°F we currently experience.

pool.q: Which greenhouse gases are exclusively human-made?
pool.explain: Other gases occur naturally and are also produced by human activities.
pool.evidence: Some, such as industrial gases, are exclusively human made.

pool.q: In the United States, where do most human-caused greenhouse gas emissions come from?
options: Burning fossil fuels — coal, natural gas and petroleum — for energy
pool.explain: About 74% of US human-caused emissions come from fossil fuel energy use.
pool.evidence: In the United States, most (about 74%) human-caused ( anthropogenic ) greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions come from burning fossil fuels—coal, natural gas, and petroleum—for energy use.

pool.q: What are the main factors that drive how much energy is consumed?
options: The number of cars and length of roads
Economic growth and weather that affects heating and cooling needs
pool.explain: Energy prices and government policies also shape which types of energy are used.
pool.evidence: weather patterns that affect heating and cooling needs are the main factors that drive the amount of energy consumed

pool.q: Why does the US EPA publish estimates of total US greenhouse gas emissions?
options: To meet annual US commitments under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
pool.explain: National inventories are reported to the UNFCCC every year.
pool.evidence: GHG emissions to meet annual U.S. commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

pool.q: What do fossil fuels mainly consist of?
pool.explain: Burning them combines the carbon with oxygen to form CO2.
pool.evidence: Fossil fuels consist mainly of carbon and hydrogen.

pool.q: Which of these belongs to the first step of developing a GHG inventory?
options: Reviewing accounting standards, setting organisational and operational boundaries, and choosing a base year
pool.explain: Boundaries and a base year make results consistent and comparable over time.
pool.evidence: Review accounting standards and methods, determine organizational and operational boundaries, and choose a base year.

pool.q: Which emissions count as scope 1?
options: Direct emissions from sources the organisation owns or controls, such as its boilers and vehicles
Emissions when customers use sold products
pool.explain: Scope 2 covers purchased energy; scope 3 covers the rest of the value chain.
pool.evidence: Scope 1 emissions are direct GHG emissions that occur from sources that are controlled or owned by an organization

pool.q: What are scope 2 emissions?
options: Indirect emissions associated with purchased electricity, steam, heat or cooling
pool.explain: Scope 1 is direct; scope 2 is purchased energy; scope 3 is the rest of the value chain.
pool.evidence: Scope 2 emissions are indirect GHG emissions associated with the purchase of electricity, steam, heat, or cooling.

pool.q: Scope 2 emissions physically happen at the power plant. Why are they counted in the buyer's inventory?
options: Because power plants do not report emissions
Because they are a result of the organisation's energy use
Because the law double-counts all emissions
Because electricity is always generated on site
pool.explain: The organisation's demand for energy causes those emissions.
pool.evidence: they are accounted for in an organization’s GHG inventory because they are a result of the organization’s energy use.

pool.q: What do scope 3 emissions include?
options: All sources not within the organisation's scope 1 and 2 boundary
pool.explain: One organisation's scope 3 is another organisation's scope 1 and 2.
pool.evidence: Scope 3 emissions include all sources not within an organization’s scope 1 and 2 boundary.

pool.q: How many scope 3 categories does an organisation screen for relevance?
pool.explain: Not every category is relevant to every organisation.
pool.evidence: a relevance assessment to determine which of the 15 categories are relevant to the reporting organization.

pool.q: How are one organisation's scope 3 emissions related to other organisations?
options: They are double counting and must be removed
They are always zero for small firms
They are the scope 1 and 2 emissions of another organisation
pool.explain: Your suppliers' direct emissions show up in your value chain.
pool.evidence: The scope 3 emissions for one organization are the scope 1 and 2 emissions of another organization.

pool.q: Why do scope 3 sources often offer emissions reduction opportunities?
options: They are fully under the organisation's control
They are the cheapest emissions to measure
They may make up most of an organisation's emissions
They never have to be reported
pool.explain: Even without control, an organisation may influence the activities that cause them.
pool.evidence: because scope 3 sources may represent most of an organization

pool.q: To fully meet GHG Protocol standards, which scope 3 emissions must be reported?
options: Emissions from all relevant scope 3 categories
pool.explain: Building a complete scope 3 inventory is a process of continuous improvement.
pool.evidence: To fully meet GHG Protocol standards, an organization must report emissions from all relevant scope 3 categories.

pool.q: Which parts of the value chain do scope 3 emissions cover?
options: Both upstream and downstream of the organisation's activities
pool.explain: Upstream includes purchased goods; downstream includes use and disposal of sold products.
pool.evidence: Scope 3 emission sources include emissions both upstream and downstream of the organization

pool.q: Why does EPA use a marginal emission factor to estimate savings from efficiency and renewable energy?
options: It is the cheapest factor to calculate
It best represents which fossil-fired units the savings displace
It is required for scope 3 only
pool.explain: Efficiency and renewables mostly displace plants brought online to meet demand, not baseload plants.
pool.evidence: A marginal emission factor is the best representation to estimate which fossil-fired units EE/RE are displacing across the fossil fleet.

pool.q: What does calculating the emission impact of efficiency and renewable energy require?
options: Measuring the efficiency of each light bulb
Estimating how much fossil-fired generation and emissions they displace
pool.explain: Savings come from fossil generation that no longer has to run.
pool.evidence: Calculating the emission impacts of EE and RE on the electricity grid requires estimating the amount of fossil-fired generation and emissions being displaced by EE and RE.

pool.q: For electricity used (not avoided), which emission factor does the calculator apply?
options: A zero factor for renewable power
A regional or national average emission factor
pool.explain: Marginal factors are for avoided electricity; average factors are for electricity consumed.
pool.evidence: This is either a regionally specific or a national average emissions factor, depending on the user input.

pool.q: What happens in the calculator if no zip code is entered?
options: The national default emission rate is used
The highest regional rate is used
A rate of zero is used
pool.explain: Entering a zip code gives a regionally specific, more accurate rate.
pool.evidence: If no zip code is entered by the user, the national default will be used

pool.q: Which greenhouse gases does the electricity equivalency calculation include?
options: All the gases in the Kyoto basket
pool.explain: Other gases from power generation are left out of this particular calculation.
pool.evidence: This calculation does not include any greenhouse gases other than CO

pool.q: How did EPA estimate the total CO2 emissions per home?
options: By measuring chimney emissions in sample homes
By surveying owners about their habits
By converting electricity, gas, fuel oil and propane use to tonnes of CO2 and adding them up
pool.explain: Each fuel has its own carbon coefficient; the results are summed per home.
pool.evidence: consumption figures were converted from their various units to metric tons of CO

pool.q: On average, how much delivered electricity did each US home use in 2022?
pool.explain: Averages like this let calculators express emissions as 'homes' energy use'.
pool.evidence: On average, each home consumed 12,194 kWh of delivered electricity.

pool.q: In the UK guidance for councils' own estate, what should each published GHG report show at a minimum?
options: Totals in CO2e for scope 1, scope 2 and scope 3 (if provided)
The names of staff who travel most
A forecast for the next 50 years
pool.explain: Publishing totals locally makes councils accountable to local people.
pool.evidence: as a minimum totals in CO2e for Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions (if provided)

pool.q: Why should councils publish the greenhouse gas emissions of their own estate?
options: So local authorities are accountable to local people for their emissions
To compete in national league tables
pool.explain: It supports the localism agenda.
pool.evidence: ensuring local authorities are accountable to their local people for their greenhouse gas emissions

pool.q: Which guidance should local authorities follow when preparing their emission reports?
options: The government guidance for businesses and organisations
The EU Emissions Trading System rules
Any method their energy supplier suggests
pool.explain: Using the same guidance as businesses keeps reports consistent and comparable.
pool.evidence: When preparing their emission reports local authorities should follow the guidance for businesses and organisations

pool.q: Who is the SECR guidance for academy trusts aimed at?
options: Chief financial officers, accounting officers and trustees
pool.explain: They are responsible for the trust's annual report and accounts.
pool.evidence: This guidance is aimed at chief financial officers, accounting officers and trustees in academy trusts.

pool.q: Which data must academy trusts use for SECR where reasonably practicable?
options: Verifiable data such as meter readings or supplier invoices
pool.explain: Verifiable data makes the reported figures auditable.
pool.evidence: Academy trusts must use verifiable data where reasonably practicable and should consider obtaining meter data or using invoices or annual statements from suppliers.

pool.q: Is fuel for trips by train, plane or taxi that the trust does not operate included in its transport figures?
options: No — procured transport services are excluded, though they may be reported separately
Only trips over 100 km are included
pool.explain: They can be reported voluntarily, for example as scope 3 emissions.
pool.evidence: This excludes where a transportation service is procured that includes an indirect payment for the fuel consumption

pool.q: An academy trust was not in scope last year. Must it report prior-year figures?
options: No, it is not required to
It must delay reporting by a year
pool.explain: Comparatives are required only once the trust has been in scope.
pool.evidence: If an academy trust was not in scope in the previous year, it is not required to report prior year figures.

pool.q: What should a trust report if it took no energy efficiency measures during the year?
options: Measures planned for next year instead
It should state that no measures were taken
pool.explain: Saying so explicitly keeps the report transparent.
pool.evidence: If no measures have been taken, this should be stated

pool.q: In the SECR worked example, which intensity ratio is chosen?
options: Total gross emissions in tonnes CO2e per pupil
pool.explain: An intensity ratio relates emissions to a measure of activity so years can be compared.
pool.evidence: The chosen intensity measurement ratio is total gross emissions in metric tonnes CO2e per pupil, the recommended ratio for the sector.

pool.q: How often are the UK government's greenhouse gas conversion factors updated?
pool.explain: Use the factors that cover the greatest part of your reporting year.
pool.evidence: The conversion factors are updated annually and are generally released each year in June.
